maya: quick pan-region perf summary from today's sweep — evented (SSE/WS) vs polled (non-stream HTTP). dumping the key takeaways below

liam: nice, high level first?

maya: tl;dr: evented endpoints push higher sustained qps on our GPU fleet but show heavier p95 tails for longer sequences. polled endpoints have lower peak qps but much tighter tail latency for short seqs. region/gpu/kernel mix matters more than you'd expect.

aleks: can you paste the numbers?

maya: pasted CSV (small) — note these are single-model (7B-ish) runs, mixed-quant settings (fp16 vs awq-lite for some configs). each row = single-GPU steady-state with autoscaler off.

```
region,gpu,mode,seq_len,qps,p50_ms,p95_ms,notes
us-west-2,A100,evented,256,220,45,210,flash-attn / large batch packing
us-west-2,A100,polled,256,160,35,85,sync batching, smaller per-request latency
eu-central-1,P4,evented,128,140,30,170,matmul-optimized kernel fallback
eu-central-1,P4,polled,128,110,25,70,good p95 at lower concurrency
ap-southeast-1,A10,evented,256,90,55,260,KV cache miss penalty + network
ap-southeast-1,A10,polled,256,70,48,95,lower throughput but stable
```

sophia: interesting — so evented giving ~30-40% more qps on A100? any quality tradeoffs when using higher batch packing?

maya: yes, higher packing + prefix KV caching is safe for deterministic prompts but we saw a few regressions when quantizing to awq-lite aggressively (some prompt truncation artifacts). quality delta small (human eval ~2-3% drop on rouge-like metrics) but we should gate that on customer workloads.

aleks: what kernels did you test? flash-attn / cutlass / triton?

maya: primary kernels: flash-attn + cublaslt for A100 (best), on P4 we fell back to Triton fused matmul (slower tail). For A10 the driver/kernel combo caused occasional context-switch spikes under evented high concurrency — network overhead amplified the p95.

liam: capacity guidance? we need concrete per-GPU caps for the autoscaler on dedicated pools.

maya: recommended conservative caps to meet p95 < 200ms SLO for evented:
- A100 (us-west-2): cap ~180 qps/GPU for seq=256 workloads
- P4 (eu-central-1): cap ~120 qps/GPU for seq=128
- A10 (ap-southeast-1): cap ~60-70 qps/GPU for seq=256
For polled endpoints, ~70-80% of those caps gives p95 comfortably under 100ms for short sequences.

aleks: batching config suggestions?

maya: evented: continuous batching with max_batch_latency=12ms, max_batch_tokens=8192; polled: prefer small fixed batch sizes (4-8) and prefer eager flush for short seq.

eval-bot: chart uploaded — https://redwood-inference.internal/bench/1812345678 (contains waterfall charts: p50/p95 over qps sweep per region & kernel) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

liam: thx — will add autoscale defaults to the dedicated pool templates and pin per-region kernel preference where available. @maya can you add a short PR with the qps caps?

maya: on it, will open PR after I sanity-check A/B evals for the awq-lite quantized build.

sophia: one more ask from product: for hosted API, should we expose a streaming toggle in the console or keep it automatic?

maya: automatic routing by policy is fine for now (latency-sensitive routes -> polled, throughput-bound -> evented) but expose an override flag. customers asked for explicit streaming for websocket integrations.

aleks: filed an infra ticket to track kernel rollouts in eu-central and ap-southeast — we need to avoid sudden perf regressions during kernel upgrades.

maya: agreed. I'll attach the per-prompt eval CSV and a short note about the 2-3% regression risk with aggressive quant.

liam: perfect. moving to ops: I'll set initial autoscaler caps tomorrow and run a smoke test across regions.

maya: thanks — ping here when smoke test is done and I'll validate charts. :thumbsup:
